name: Grand Hyatt Fukuoka
positioning: Hotel in Fukuoka's Hakata district, connected to Canal City Hakata, with East meets West rooms and ryokan-style Japanese suites
best_for: Travelers who want direct access to Canal City Hakata's shopping and entertainment
Families who want a ryokan-style Japanese suite with futon bedding
Visitors who want to walk to Kushida Shrine and other Hakata cultural sites

facts.text: Grand Hyatt Fukuoka is in the Hakata district in the heart of Fukuoka City.
The hotel is connected to Canal City Hakata, a complex of business, entertainment and shopping facilities.
Rooms and suites embody an East meets West style.
Depending on the room type, rooms have city views or views of Canal City Hakata.
Rooms have spacious bathrooms with large tubs and separate showers.
The Hakata Suite has a Tea Bar, a dining table with integrated tea-making facilities and interiors inspired by local art and craftsmanship.
The Japanese Suite is a ryokan-style room with futon sleeping on Japanese-style bedding, recommended for families.
The Presidential Suite has living, dining and work areas and a full kitchen.
The hotel has an indoor swimming pool.
AN SPA FUKUOKA, in Club Olympus, offers aroma oil and Shiatsu massage treatments.
THE MARKET F restaurant centers on an open kitchen and charcoal grill.
Bar Fizz serves cocktails, wines and spirits with live music.

highlights.text: From the hinoki soaking tub in the Japanese Deluxe Suite, guests can view a private Japanese garden.
The Japanese Deluxe Suite has a Japanese tea ceremony room plus two tatami-mat rooms.
The first floor of Canal City Hakata is connected to the hotel's lobby level.
Kushida Shrine, Sumiyoshi Shrine, the Rakusuien Japanese garden and the Hakata Machiya Folk Museum are all within a few minutes' walk.
The Grand Club lounge on the 5th floor serves breakfast, refreshments and an evening cocktail hour for Grand Club room and suite guests.

considerations.text: Several standard and Club Access rooms are for up to two adults, and rollaway beds cannot be used in them.
WhataHotel notes an urban setting within a busy commercial complex.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
